references.text: The same rule about washing clothes and being unclean until evening applies to the one who carries the carcass of an unclean animal.
Repeats the instruction to wash clothes and be unclean until evening for the one who eats or carries a dead animal that died naturally.
Similar cleansing instructions to wash clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Concerns the one who eats animals that died naturally and must wash their clothes and bathe; otherwise they bear their guilt.
The one who touches dead bodies must wash their clothes and is unclean until evening.
Regulations about being unclean until evening and washing clothes in connection with the water of cleansing.
Repeats the prohibition against eating animals that died naturally, which is the basis for the impurity laws in Leviticus.
Ezekiel repeats the priests' purity laws regarding contact with dead bodies and subsequent cleansing.
